metadata.title: PitchCraft — Marketing Presentation Engine
metadata.objective: Position PitchCraft as the engine that replaces bullet-dump AI decks
metadata.desired_action: Install the skill and run it on a workspace

narrative.structure: Problem -> Insight -> Solution -> Product -> Proof -> Ask
arc: tension: AI decks are easy to spot
proof: this deck is the demo
ask: point your agent at a workspace

slides.message: PitchCraft turns a workspace into a marketing-grade deck.
slides.title: PitchCraft
slides.subtitle: The marketing presentation engine — sources, brand, fonts and data in; validated, art-directed deck out.

content.text: Built, validated and QA-looped by the engine it describes.

slides.speaker_notes: Open cold: every AI team can generate slides; almost none can generate a deck. PitchCraft is the difference.

slides.message: AI decks are easy to generate — and easy to spot.
slides.title: AI decks are easy to generate — and easy to spot.

content.text: Giant title. Three generic bullets. The same card grid, five slides running. Unsourced numbers. That is what 'prompt, bullets, slides' produces — and audiences have learned to see it.

slides.speaker_notes: Let the sentence sit. Everyone in the room has sat through this deck.

slides.message: A slide lands its idea in ~3 seconds or it fails.
slides.title: 3 seconds

items.label: to land a slide's core idea — the 3-second rule behind every layout decision

content.text: One slide = one primary communication job. The job lives in the Slide DSL as a written message; if the sentence cannot be written, the slide is not designed yet.

slides.speaker_notes: The DSL enforces the message field — this is a structural guarantee, not a style hope.

slides.message: Bullets-on-slides is a content dump; a deck is a communication system.
slides.title: Content dump vs communication system

items.label: Problem
items.title: Prompt → bullets → slides
items.text: No story spine, no provenance, no QA. The tool fills space; the message never lands.

items.label: Solution
items.title: Workspace → story → system → QA
items.text: Ingest sources with provenance, pick a narrative spine, serialize a validated Slide DSL, render, then inspect-repair until nothing FAILs.

slides.speaker_notes: The left column is a workflow; the right column is an engine. Same model, different system.

slides.message: Six engine layers turn material into argument.
slides.title: Six layers, one moat

items.label: L1
items.title: Source intelligence
items.text: Claims extracted with provenance; never fabricated

items.label: L2
items.title: Story intelligence
items.text: Narrative spine plus a designed emotional arc

items.label: L3
items.title: Slide DSL
items.text: Content separated from rendering; one format, many outputs

items.label: L4
items.title: Visual strategy
items.text: 16 treatments chosen by intent, never decorative

items.label: L5
items.title: Multi-renderer
items.text: HTML, PPTX and PDF from the same deck.json

items.label: L6
items.title: Visual QA loop
items.text: Inspect, repair, re-render until nothing FAILs

slides.speaker_notes: Any one layer is a nice-to-have; the six together are the moat.

slides.message: Ten phases, zero skipped steps, checkpoint artifacts in output/.
slides.title: The ten-phase pipeline

items.label: P0
items.title: Discover
items.text: Workspace inventory + tool check

items.label: P1
items.title: Ingest
items.text: Extract claims + provenance

items.label: P2-3
items.title: Story
items.text: Brief, spine, emotional arc

items.label: P4-5
items.title: Plan & DSL
items.text: slide-plan → deck.json, validated

items.label: P6-7
items.title: Theme & render
items.text: Tokens, assets, HTML/PPTX

items.label: P8-9
items.title: QA & export
items.text: Inspect-repair loop, previews

slides.speaker_notes: Nothing renders before the plan validates — that ordering is the whole trick.

slides.message: The taxonomy does the choosing — layouts picked by intent, never random.
slides.title: Intent does the choosing

content.text: 31 semantic slide types map onto 22 renderer layouts and 16 visual strategies; charts draw from 7 types keyed to analytical purpose.

chart_spec.title: What ships in the v1 contracts (counted from schemas)
chart_spec.takeaway: A taxonomy this wide means the layout follows the slide's job — the model never free-styles structure.

slides.speaker_notes: These are countable facts from the repo's schema enums — not marketing numbers.

slides.message: Same agent, different system: quality is structural.
slides.title: Same agent, different system

items.label: Before
items.title: Generated filler
items.text: Giant titles · generic bullets · repeated card grids · unsourced numbers · no QA gate · nothing editable

items.label: After
items.title: Art-directed system
items.text: One job per slide · intent-chosen layouts · on-slide sources · PASS/WARNING/FAIL gate · deck.json stays editable

slides.speaker_notes: The right column is not effort — it is structure. The gate makes the floor the minimum.

slides.message: This deck is the demo — built by the engine it pitches.
slides.title: The deck is the demo

content.text: Challenge: prove the engine publicly, on itself.

items: Approach: this deck runs the full pipeline on its own specification
Sources: every claim cites a section of the distilled spec
Design: default editorial tokens, information design only — no generated images

slides.speaker_notes: Dogfooding as evidence: the artifacts in output/ are the audit trail — slide-plan, sources-map, qa-report.

slides.message: An engine, not a one-off generator.
slides.title: The mandate

content.text: Build this as a reusable AI presentation engine, not a one-off slide generator.

slides.speaker_notes: The spec's own words. This is the standard the repo holds itself to.

slides.message: HTML, PPTX, PDF and the DSL ship today.
slides.title: What you can run with

items.label: Now
items.title: Render + export
items.text: Self-contained deck.html; editable PPTX (pptxgenjs); PDF via print mode; preview PNGs feed the QA loop

items.label: Now
items.title: The deck's DNA
items.text: deck.json is the source of truth — re-render any format, any time, from the same DSL

items.label: Optional
items.title: Calibrated AI QA
items.text: TypeSafe Score/Noul judgments advise the QA loop when an API key is present — humans keep the final PASS

slides.speaker_notes: Adoption is one command; the DSL means you are never locked into one renderer.

slides.message: Point your agent at a workspace and say the word.
slides.title: Point your agent at a workspace and say the word.

items.label: Install
items.title: npx skills add kanomwhandev/pitchcraft
items.text: Any skills-compatible agent

items.label: Run
items.title: "Create a 12-slide deck from this workspace"
items.text: Audience, goal, style — the pipeline does the rest

items.label: Keep
items.title: deck.json stays yours
items.text: The DSL is the deliverable; formats are views

slides.speaker_notes: Close on the command. The next deck they see should be theirs.
